source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Isolated lumbar muscle soreness because radicular sensory symptoms exclude nerve-root involvement","B":"Lumbar radiculopathy, often from disc herniation compressing or irritating a spinal nerve root","C":"Acute appendicitis because unilateral leg paresthesia is a typical manifestation of appendiceal inflammation","D":"Venous insufficiency because lumbar movement commonly causes dermatomal numbness from venous reflux"}}
source_row.rationale: Sciatica is a clinical pattern of radicular pain that may include numbness, tingling, or weakness along the affected nerve distribution. Lumbar disc herniation is a common cause of nerve-root compression or inflammation.
source_row.source_detail: Clinical presentation and common causes including disc herniation; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client has low-back pain radiating down one leg with numbness and tingling in a nerve-root distribution. Which condition is most consistent?
